name: Python Programming
description: A draft progression from Python basics to functions, files, and reliable error handling.

resources.title: Python Fundamentals: visual preview
resources.body: Draft storyboard activity: sketch and narrate one core python fundamentals idea; this label does not refer to a published video.

resources.title: Python Fundamentals: guided practice
resources.body: Original self-guided activity: work through a short python fundamentals example and check each reasoning step; this is a learning prompt, not an external resource.

questions.text: What value does the expression 2 + 3 * 4 produce?
questions.explanation: Multiplication has higher precedence than addition, so 2 + 12 = 14.

questions.text: Which literal creates a string containing the word hello?
questions.explanation: Text literals are quoted; the quotes are syntax, not part of the value.

questions.text: After x = 7; x += 2, what is x?
questions.explanation: The augmented assignment adds 2 to the existing value 7.

questions.text: What does type(3.0) report in standard Python?
questions.explanation: A numeric literal with a decimal point is a float.

questions.text: Which expression tests whether n is an even integer?
questions.explanation: An even integer has remainder zero when divided by 2.

questions.text: What is the value of bool(0)?
questions.explanation: Zero is a falsy numeric value in Python.

questions.text: Which statement assigns the value 12 to a variable named count?
questions.explanation: The assignment operator is a single equals sign with the variable on the left.

questions.text: What is the result of "py" + "thon"?
questions.explanation: The + operator concatenates two strings directly.

resources.title: Conditions and Loops: visual preview
resources.body: Draft storyboard activity: sketch and narrate one core conditions and loops idea; this label does not refer to a published video.

resources.title: Conditions and Loops: guided practice
resources.body: Original self-guided activity: work through a short conditions and loops example and check each reasoning step; this is a learning prompt, not an external resource.

questions.text: Which keyword begins a conditional branch in Python?
questions.explanation: Python uses if to begin a conditional statement.

questions.text: How many times does for i in range(3) execute its body?
questions.explanation: range(3) yields 0, 1, and 2: three values.

questions.text: What values are produced by range(2, 7, 2)?
questions.explanation: The start is included, the stop is excluded, and the step is 2.

questions.text: What does break do inside a loop?
questions.explanation: break terminates the innermost loop immediately.

questions.text: What is printed by: for i in range(3): print(i, end="") ?
questions.explanation: range(3) yields 0, 1, and 2 in ascending order.

questions.text: Which value makes if not value: execute its body?
questions.explanation: An empty string is falsy, so not value evaluates to True.

questions.text: What does continue do in a loop?
options: Skips the rest of this iteration
questions.explanation: continue advances to the next iteration without running the remaining body.

questions.text: What is the final value of total? total=0; for n in [1,2,3]: total += n
questions.explanation: The loop accumulates 1 + 2 + 3, giving 6.

resources.body: Draft storyboard activity: sketch and narrate one core collections and iteration idea; this label does not refer to a published video.

resources.title: Collections and Iteration: guided practice
resources.body: Original self-guided activity: work through a short collections and iteration example and check each reasoning step; this is a learning prompt, not an external resource.

questions.text: Which Python collection is ordered and mutable?
questions.explanation: A list preserves element order and can be modified.
Python sequences use zero-based indexing, so index 1 selects the second item.

questions.text: What does {"a": 1}["a"] return?
questions.explanation: Dictionary indexing by an existing key returns its associated value.

questions.text: What is len({2, 2, 3})?
questions.explanation: Sets keep unique elements, leaving 2 and 3.

questions.text: Which expression creates a new list of squares for values in nums?
questions.explanation: A list comprehension evaluates x**2 for each item in nums.

questions.text: What does tuple([1, 2]) produce?
questions.explanation: tuple converts the iterable into an immutable tuple.

questions.text: If d = {"x": 4}, which test checks whether "x" is a key?
questions.explanation: Membership testing on a dictionary checks keys by default.

questions.text: What does list(enumerate(["a", "b"])) return?
questions.explanation: enumerate pairs each item with its zero-based index by default.

resources.title: Functions and Scope: visual preview
resources.body: Draft storyboard activity: sketch and narrate one core functions and scope idea; this label does not refer to a published video.

resources.title: Functions and Scope: guided practice
resources.body: Original self-guided activity: work through a short functions and scope example and check each reasoning step; this is a learning prompt, not an external resource.

questions.text: Which keyword defines a function in Python?
questions.explanation: A named function definition begins with def.

questions.text: What does return 5 do in a function?
questions.explanation: return supplies a result to the caller and ends that function call.

questions.text: If def add(a, b=2): return a+b, what is add(3)?
questions.explanation: The omitted b argument uses its default value 2.

questions.text: What is the result of calling a function that reaches its end without return?
questions.explanation: A function that returns no explicit value implicitly returns None.

questions.text: Why can a mutable list used as a default argument cause surprises?
options: Python copies it on each call
The same default object is reused across calls
Defaults are evaluated after every call
questions.explanation: Default expressions are evaluated once when the def statement runs.

questions.text: What does len("cat") return?
questions.explanation: The string contains three characters.

questions.text: Which statement makes a local name refer to a module-level variable for assignment?
questions.explanation: global declares that assignments to x use the module-level binding.

questions.text: A function accepts *args. What does args contain inside the function?
options: A tuple of extra positional arguments
A list of all local variables
questions.explanation: *args collects any extra positional arguments into a tuple.

resources.title: Modules and Files: visual preview
resources.body: Draft storyboard activity: sketch and narrate one core modules and files idea; this label does not refer to a published video.

resources.title: Modules and Files: guided practice
resources.body: Original self-guided activity: work through a short modules and files example and check each reasoning step; this is a learning prompt, not an external resource.

questions.text: Which statement imports Python’s math module?
questions.explanation: The import statement loads a module into the current namespace.

questions.text: After import math, how do you call the square-root function?
questions.explanation: The module name qualifies its exported function.

questions.text: What is the purpose of if __name__ == "__main__":?
options: It runs a block only when the file is executed as the program
questions.explanation: When run directly, the module’s __name__ is set to "__main__".

questions.text: Why is with open("data.txt") as f commonly used?
options: It ensures the file is closed when the block exits
It makes the file read-only permanently
questions.explanation: A with statement manages the file context and closes it when leaving the block.

questions.text: Which mode opens an existing text file for appending?
questions.explanation: Append mode adds writes at the end without truncating existing contents.

questions.text: Which standard-library module provides JSON parsing?
questions.explanation: The json module encodes and decodes JSON data.

questions.text: What does pathlib.Path("notes.txt").suffix return?
questions.explanation: The suffix property returns the final extension including its leading dot.

questions.text: What is a benefit of importing a module with import package.tool?
options: Its names are isolated under package.tool
questions.explanation: Qualified imports keep names under a module namespace and reduce collisions.

resources.title: Exceptions and Testing: visual preview
resources.body: Draft storyboard activity: sketch and narrate one core exceptions and testing idea; this label does not refer to a published video.

resources.title: Exceptions and Testing: guided practice
resources.body: Original self-guided activity: work through a short exceptions and testing example and check each reasoning step; this is a learning prompt, not an external resource.

questions.text: Which keyword begins an exception-handling block?
questions.explanation: A try block contains code whose exceptions may be handled.

questions.text: Which exception is raised by 1 / 0?
questions.explanation: Division by zero for numeric values raises ZeroDivisionError.

questions.text: What does an except ValueError clause do?
options: Runs only when no exception occurs
questions.explanation: The handler runs when the protected code raises a matching ValueError.

questions.text: What is the purpose of a finally block?
options: Run cleanup code whether or not an exception occurred
questions.explanation: finally is used for cleanup that should occur after try/except processing.

questions.text: Which assertion tests that double(3) equals 6 in a simple unit test?
questions.explanation: Python’s assert statement raises AssertionError if the condition is false.

questions.text: What does raising an exception communicate?
questions.explanation: Exceptions signal that normal processing cannot continue as written.

questions.text: Why should a handler often catch a specific exception rather than bare except?
options: To avoid handling unrelated failures accidentally
questions.explanation: Specific handlers limit recovery logic to errors it knows how to address.

questions.text: In pytest, what does a test function name usually begin with?
questions.explanation: Pytest’s default discovery recognizes functions whose names start with test_.
